title: A code validator that compiles and runs the code it is validating: decorators execute at definition time
index_line: T-0026 · CODE_EXEC · 'validate this snippet' endpoint compiles+execs it; a decorator is an expression, so it runs · python/any-embedded-Python · corroborated
invariant_violated: An endpoint that *validates* user code is assumed to be inert because it never calls the validated function. But validation that uses the language's own compiler and executes the definition is execution: a function definition carries its decorators, decorators are arbitrary expressions, and expressions are evaluated when the definition is built.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated request posts a code snippet to the validation endpoint, which exists so users can check their flow definitions
the endpoint parses the snippet and extracts the import and function-definition nodes it intends to check
imports are merely resolved; function definitions are compiled and executed to confirm they are well-formed
the definition's decorator expressions are evaluated as part of building that definition, before any call to the function
the decorator body runs with the privileges of the service, and the endpoint helpfully returns the captured output inside the error it reports

source.http.body.value: the JSON `code` field of the validate endpoint — no auth, no token; the endpoint is only *supposed* to be used by logged-in flow builders

sink.eval.value: compile()+exec() over an AST-extracted definition, or any 'parse then run to check' path (ast+exec, vm.runInNewContext, eval of a function body)

oracle.error.value: the validator returns the exception it caught, so the command output comes back in the HTTP response — a single-request, fully-blind-free RCE

guard.none.value: no sandbox, no allow-list on decorator expressions; the validator's whole purpose is to touch hostile input

preconditions.expr: the validation/format-check endpoint is reachable without authentication
the validator compiles and executes what it parses rather than only parsing it
decorators or default-argument expressions survive the AST walk and are evaluated

check.spec: send a definition whose decorator is a side-effecting expression (a write to /tmp) and check for the side effect without calling the function

success: command output returns in the HTTP response through the reported error, with no login and no cookie
the effect happens without the posted function ever being called — the decorator fired during validation
a marker file appears on the server from a request that only 'validated' code
failure_like: the validator only parses (ast.parse without compile/exec) — nothing is evaluated
execution happens in a subprocess/isolate with no filesystem or network, so the decorator is inert in practice
false_positive: a 200 saying the code is valid — that is the endpoint working, not exploitation; require a side effect
an error mentioning `exec` in a traceback because the *validator itself* failed, not because the payload ran
client-side validation in the browser — not this, the payload must reach the server

hazards: the endpoint is deliberately loud about errors, which makes it the cheapest possible RCE oracle — never treat 'it just validates' as low risk
decorators are not the only definition-time hook: default arguments, base-class expressions and annotations are all evaluated when the definition is built
this class is invisible to auth-based triage because the endpoint is designed to be pre-auth for builders; triage by 'does it exec', not by 'who can reach it'
logging may be off by default (no access log), so exploitation can be silent — check upstream proxies, not the app
non_transfers: validators that only parse (no compile/exec) or that run in a separate process with no capabilities
schema/AST allow-list validation that never hands the snippet to the interpreter
